title: Passengers, Cargo, Groups & Night
summary: Extra weight from a passenger or heavy load changes handling, balance, acceleration and stopping distance, so practice with light loads first.
Massachusetts law requires every motorcycle passenger to wear a US DOT approved helmet.
A passenger should mount only after the engine is running, sit close without interfering with control, hold the rider's waist or hips, and keep feet on the footpegs even when stopped.
Passengers should stay directly behind the rider, lean with the rider in turns, and keep talking and moving to a minimum.
With a passenger, leave a bigger space cushion for slowing and stopping, and adjust speed on rough, sloped or curved roads; suspension and tire pressure may need adjusting.
Secure cargo low and over the axles; loads behind the rear axle upset balance and affect braking, and saddlebag loads should be balanced side to side; elastic cords help keep loads from shifting.
If a group has more than five or six riders, split it into two smaller groups.
Put inexperienced riders toward the front of a group, where more experienced riders can watch them; make sure everyone knows the route, and signal lane changes early.

Ride in a staggered formation: the leader on the left side of the lane, the second rider just behind on the right, and at least two seconds between each rider and the one directly ahead in the same track. Switch to single file for curves, turns and freeway entry or exit, and avoid pairing up side by side.
When a staggered group passes a vehicle, riders pass one at a time, starting with the leader.
At night, slow down, use your headlight fully and increase following distance; Massachusetts requires headlights from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise.
When pulling off the road, signal early, check that the surface is firm, slow down on soft shoulders, park well away from traffic, and use care with the kickstand on soft or sloped ground.

questions.q: Under Massachusetts law, what must every motorcycle passenger wear?
options: A US DOT approved helmet
Eye protection only
A reflective vest
Over-the-ankle boots
questions.explanation: Massachusetts requires all passengers to wear a helmet approved by the US DOT. Protective clothing and face protection are recommended on top of that.

questions.q: When should a passenger climb onto the motorcycle?
options: Before the rider gets on
Before the engine is started
After the engine has been started
Only after the rider has started moving slowly
questions.explanation: The manual says passengers should get on after the engine is already running.

questions.q: Where should a passenger keep their feet while the motorcycle is stopped?
options: On the ground to help balance the bike
Firmly on the footpegs
Resting on the rear frame
Wherever is most comfortable
questions.explanation: Passengers should keep their feet planted on the footpegs at all times, including at stops.

questions.q: How should a passenger behave in turns and curves?
options: Lean the opposite way to keep the bike upright
Sit upright even as the rider leans into the turn
Shift to the outside of the seat
Stay directly behind the rider and lean with the rider
questions.explanation: The passenger should stay in line behind the rider and lean along with the rider through turns.

questions.q: When carrying a passenger, how should you change the way you stop or slow down?
options: Brake later, since the extra weight adds traction
Leave a larger space cushion
Use only the rear brake
Make no change; stopping is unaffected
questions.explanation: The added weight changes how the bike handles and stops, so the manual says to allow more space when slowing or stopping.

questions.q: If you need to talk to your passenger while riding, what does the manual suggest?
options: Turn your head fully around so the passenger can hear you clearly
Pull over every time
Turn your head slightly while keeping your focus on the road ahead
Have the passenger lean forward over your shoulder
questions.explanation: A slight head turn is suggested, as long as you keep watching the road and traffic ahead.

questions.q: What adjustments may be needed on the motorcycle when carrying a passenger?
options: Minor changes to suspension and tire pressure
Moving the rider's seating position far forward
Removing the mirrors
Raising the handlebars above shoulder height
questions.explanation: Depending on the passenger's weight, small suspension and tire pressure adjustments may be needed. The manual also says riders should not have to change their own seating position.

questions.q: Where is the best place to carry cargo on a motorcycle?
options: High on the rear seat frame
Behind the rear axle
On the handlebars
Low and over the wheel axles
questions.explanation: Keeping loads low and over the axles keeps the bike stable. Loads behind the rear axle hurt balance and braking.

questions.q: What can happen if saddlebags are loaded unevenly?
options: The motorcycle may pull to one side
The turn signals may stop flashing
The engine may overheat
The horn may stop working
questions.explanation: An uneven load between the bags can make the motorcycle pull toward one side, so keep the weight in each bag about the same.

questions.q: What danger does overloading saddlebags create?
options: Bags squeezing the fuel line and starving the engine of fuel
Bags catching in the wheel or chain and locking the rear wheel
Bags pressing on the throttle cable so the throttle sticks open
Bags jamming the shift lever so you cannot change gears
questions.explanation: Overloaded bags can get caught in the wheel or chain, which can lock the rear wheel and cause a skid.

questions.q: A group of eight motorcyclists wants to ride together. What does the manual recommend?
options: Ride side by side in pairs
Ride as one group with the newest riders at the back
Split into two separate groups
Ride as one group in single file at all times
questions.explanation: When a group grows beyond five or six riders, it should be divided into two smaller groups.

questions.q: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?
options: At the very back
In a separate group made up of other new riders
Side by side with an experienced rider who can coach them
Toward the front, where experienced riders can watch them
questions.explanation: The manual says to place newer riders near the front so more experienced riders behind them can keep an eye on them.

questions.q: In a staggered formation, what is the minimum gap between the first rider and the third rider, who follows in the same track?
options: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds
questions.explanation: The manual puts the third rider directly behind the leader, at least two seconds back, and the fourth rider the same distance behind the second; the Staggering diagram on p.33 marks both gaps as two seconds. The manual gives no figure for the diagonal gap to the second rider.

questions.q: When should a group switch from a staggered formation to single file?
options: When approaching turns or curves and when entering or exiting freeways
On long, straight stretches of road and while cruising on freeways
Whenever traffic is light and there are no other vehicles nearby
Only when the group is stopped at traffic lights or stop signs
questions.explanation: Riders should leave the stagger and ride single file for turns and curves and when getting on or off freeways. The rest of the time, including straight roads and the freeway itself, the manual recommends the staggered formation.

questions.q: How should a group in staggered formation pass another vehicle?
options: All riders pass at the same time
The last rider passes first, then the others move up
Riders pair up side by side and pass together
One rider at a time, starting with the leader
questions.explanation: When there is room, the leader passes first and promptly returns to the original lane; each remaining rider then passes the same way, one at a time. Once past, riders keep their original lane positions.

questions.q: Under Massachusetts law, when must motorcyclists use their headlights?
options: From sunset to sunrise
From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
From one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise
Only when streetlights are off
questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires headlights from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise, so the legal requirement starts 30 minutes after sunset, not at sunset. Beyond the law, the manual recommends always riding with your headlight on (p.20).
